name: Argyll Data Development Ltd
ownership_summary: Private company incorporated 17 Feb 2023, registered at Killellan Farm. Active directors: Peter Griffiths (executive chairman), Robert Lyle Mitchell (landowner/farmer), Brian Michael Bowen. Two directors appointed Aug 2024 resigned 1 Apr 2026.
notes: Lead promoter of the Killellan AI Growth Zone bid and SambaNova partnership. A very small SPV-scale company, not an established data centre developer.

name: Argyll Energy Development Ltd
ownership_summary: Private company incorporated 16 Feb 2023, registered at Killellan Farm; directors Peter Griffiths and Robert Lyle Mitchell.
notes: Co-promoter responsible for the energy strand of the AI Growth Zone bid.

name: Argyll Infrastructure Holdings Limited (AIH)
ownership_summary: Incorporated 17 Nov 2025 in Dunoon. Press describes AIH as the funding vehicle: £15m initial raise (Dec 2025), £100m in negotiation, €2bn target with European Guarantee Services and Ocorian AIFM (Luxembourg). Press claims AIH was 'founded in 2023', contradicted by the Companies House incorporation date.
notes: Holds a stated three-year exclusivity agreement with SambaNova; relationship to the two 2023 development companies not established from filings.

name: SambaNova Systems
notes: October 2025 'strategic partnership' to deliver a renewable-powered sovereign AI inference cloud using SN40L (and later SN50) systems. This is a partnership/exclusivity and equipment-order arrangement, not a commitment to build or fund the Killellan campus; the cloud launched in May 2026 runs from other undisclosed UK data centres. SambaNova raised $350m Series E in early 2026.

name: Robert Lyle Mitchell (via Cowal Sand & Gravel Ltd.)
ownership_summary: The AI Growth Zone bid states surface and mineral rights are held by Mr Robert Mitchell; Cowal Sand & Gravel Ltd. (inc. 2004, registered at Killellan Farm, SIC 08120 sand/gravel pits) operates the quarry and made quarry applications. Mitchell was the applicant for 20/00229/PP and 25/00445/CLAWU and is a director of both Argyll development companies.

name: Schneider Electric
notes: Named consortium partner in the AI Growth Zone bid (microgrid design, UPS/cooling, EcoStruxure). Level of contractual commitment not disclosed.

name: Lenovo
notes: Named consortium partner in the bid (HPC systems). Level of contractual commitment not disclosed; not mentioned in the later SambaNova announcements.

name: CorPower Ocean
notes: Preferred wave-energy partner; Pre-FEED for a 600 MW wave array off the west coast near Islay, with a stated 2 GW ambition. Technology at pre-commercial stage.

name: Invinity Energy Systems
notes: Vanadium flow battery supplier named in the bid.

name: Suir Engineering
notes: Named engineering partner (hyperscale M&E track record).

name: Commsworld
notes: Fibre connectivity partner; letter in the bid proposes two diverse 100Gb waves, requiring new fibre builds Kilchattan Bay-Rothesay (~8 miles) and Innellan exchange to the site (~6 miles, landowner permissions needed) — i.e. the site currently lacks diverse high-capacity fibre.

name: Argyll and Bute Council
notes: Named in the bid as a local governance partner; also the planning authority. No formal council position on the campus located.

name: Action to Protect Rural Scotland (APRS)
notes: Campaigns against hyperscale data centres in rural Scotland; maintains a page on this project (under the name 'Killean') highlighting the absence of a planning application for the 74 ha site, and runs a 'Stop the Hyperscale AI Data Centres' petition.
